time.rule: The agent expresses semantic time; the compiler produces physical time. Write an anchor, never a frame.

forms.means: An edge of one beat, optionally nudged by a rhythm token. Use it for the two moments a beat genuinely has: where it begins and where it ends. There is no midpoint form, because the middle of a beat is a fraction of a duration rather than a moment anyone wrote, and which word it falls on cannot be known until the take is recorded. Rhythm tokens are absolute frame counts, not fractions of the beat, so this form reaches about a second in from either edge; anywhere else inside the beat, name a word. `scene` is a pseudo-beat meaning the scene’s own bounds.

forms.expectation: naming a word the beat actually speaks (no offset)
forms.means: The frame the narrator begins that word. Open to any event whose moment is justified by a sentence: name the word that opens the justifying clause. An action listing `deicticFields` must use this form for those payload fields — that is an obligation on pointing gestures, never a permission gate on every other event. Two events that both name a word fire in the order their words are spoken, which you can read off the beat text you wrote — so when the events of a scene must not overtake one another, anchor all of them by word. The word must appear in that beat’s text exactly once — twice is an error, not a first match — and takes no offset, because an offset from a word onset is the arithmetic this form exists to avoid: if the event belongs slightly later, name the next word. `scene` has no text, so it cannot carry this form.

UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY.means: A scene names a capability that the catalog does not publish.
UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY.repair: Choose a capability id from catalog.capabilities and rewrite the scene for it.

INVALID_PROPS.means: A scene property does not satisfy the selected capability schema.
INVALID_PROPS.repair: Use the reported field and expected values to make props match that schema.

UNKNOWN_ACTION.means: An event names an action the selected capability does not support.
UNKNOWN_ACTION.repair: Choose an action from the capability actions, or remove the event.

UNKNOWN_LAYOUT.means: A scene selects a layout that its capability does not publish.
UNKNOWN_LAYOUT.repair: Replace it with one of the capability layouts listed in expected.

INVALID_PAYLOAD.means: An event payload is absent when required or fails its action schema.
INVALID_PAYLOAD.repair: Author the payload from the action payloadSchema and the reported field details.

UNKNOWN_ANCHOR.means: An event anchor is malformed or points outside the beats available to its scene.
UNKNOWN_ANCHOR.repair: Use catalog.time forms and anchor the event to scene or to a beat the scene spans.

AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR.means: A word anchor names text that occurs more than once in the same beat.
AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR.repair: Split or rephrase the beat, or use an unambiguous boundary anchor.

DEICTIC_ANCHOR_REQUIRED.means: A pointing action does not land while the narration says the value it identifies.
DEICTIC_ANCHOR_REQUIRED.repair: Move the event to one of the word anchors listed in expected.

EVENT_BEFORE_ELEMENT_REVEALED.means: An event acts on an element the plan has not brought onto the frame yet.
EVENT_BEFORE_ELEMENT_REVEALED.repair: Move the reveal to an earlier anchor, or move this event to one at or after it.

EVENT_EXCEEDS_CONTENT.means: A scene lists more advancing events than its own content has steps to take, so the last of them move nothing on the frame.
EVENT_EXCEEDS_CONTENT.repair: Remove the surplus events, or lengthen the content they step through until there is a step for each one.

EVENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH.means: An advancing event names a narration step different from the content step it changes.
EVENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH.repair: Make the word anchor name the corresponding content word, or use a beat boundary for coarse pacing.

EVENTS_OUT_OF_ORDER.means: A scene lists its events in one order and they resolve to frames in another.
EVENTS_OUT_OF_ORDER.repair: Move the overtaking event to a later anchor, or reorder the list so it reads in the order it plays.

UNKNOWN_SLOT.means: A persistent element requests a placement slot outside the public slot vocabulary.
UNKNOWN_SLOT.repair: Choose a slot listed in expected and revalidate the plan.

BELOW_MIN_DURATION.means: A compiled scene is too short to perform its capability animation safely.
BELOW_MIN_DURATION.repair: Give the scene more narration time, usually by merging adjacent beats into its span.

MISSING_ASSET_REFERENCE.means: A scene that requires media has no authored asset requirement to resolve.
MISSING_ASSET_REFERENCE.repair: Add the required asset-reference field described by the capability schema.

MALFORMED_PLAN.means: The plan JSON does not have the required VideoPlan structure or field types.
MALFORMED_PLAN.repair: Repair the reported structural field using the published VideoPlan JSON Schema.

DUPLICATE_ID.means: Two authored objects reuse an id that must be unique in its plan scope.
DUPLICATE_ID.repair: Rename one duplicate and update every reference to it.

BEAT_NOT_CONTIGUOUS.means: A section or scene claims beats that are separated in narration order.
BEAT_NOT_CONTIGUOUS.repair: Make spansBeats one uninterrupted ordered range, or split the claimant.

BEAT_DOUBLE_BOOKED.means: More than one section or scene claims the same narration beat.
BEAT_DOUBLE_BOOKED.repair: Assign that beat to exactly one claimant by adjusting their spansBeats arrays.

BEAT_UNCOVERED.means: A narration beat belongs to no section or to no scene within its section.
BEAT_UNCOVERED.repair: Extend or add one claimant so every beat is covered exactly once.

EMPTY_BEAT_SPAN.means: A section or scene claims no narration beats and therefore has no duration.
EMPTY_BEAT_SPAN.repair: Assign at least one beat, or remove the empty section or scene.

SCENE_CUTS_MID_SENTENCE.means: A scene boundary interrupts a sentence before the narration reaches its end.
SCENE_CUTS_MID_SENTENCE.repair: Move the boundary to a sentence end or keep the sentence in one scene.

MISSING_BEAT_TIMING.means: The verified Take contains no timing for a beat present in the plan.
MISSING_BEAT_TIMING.repair: Restore the matching plan and Take, or record a new Take for the changed narration.

INVALID_TIMING_INPUT.means: Take timings are invalid or are not a faithful projection of the current plan.
INVALID_TIMING_INPUT.repair: Do not edit timings; verify the Take binding and record again when it is stale.

SOFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.means: A value is outside a capability recommendation but still satisfies its hard schema.
SOFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.repair: Follow the situated suggestion when visual quality matters; the plan may still ship.

SLOT_RELOCATED.means: The compiler moved a persistent element to avoid an unsafe or occupied placement.
SLOT_RELOCATED.repair: Accept the safe placement, or choose a conflict-free preferred slot.

NARRATION_NAMES_COLLAPSED_VALUE.means: Narration or event text names a value this scene collapsed, so the words describe something the frame does not show.
NARRATION_NAMES_COLLAPSED_VALUE.repair: Keep the value on screen by freeing the region the scene occupies, or rewrite the text so it does not name a value the scene does not draw.

CAPACITY_REDUCED_BY_COMPOSITION.means: A scene yielded into a composition that holds fewer values than the full canvas, so the weakest were collapsed and are not on screen.
CAPACITY_REDUCED_BY_COMPOSITION.repair: Free the region the scene occupies by placing the contending element in a slot the scene does not use, choose a layout the composition holds more of, or shorten the series to what the composition holds.

PERSISTENT_ELEMENT_HIDDEN.means: No safe placement remained, so a persistent element is absent for part of the render.
PERSISTENT_ELEMENT_HIDDEN.repair: Reduce simultaneous elements or change their requested placements.

ASSET_PLACEHOLDER.means: Required media is represented by a placeholder because resolution is pending or failed.
ASSET_PLACEHOLDER.repair: Resolve a pending requirement, or fix the reported failed asset before final delivery.

MOTION_PROFILE_REPETITION.means: Adjacent scenes repeat a motion profile often enough to make pacing feel mechanical.
MOTION_PROFILE_REPETITION.repair: Vary a scene motionProfile while keeping its intended editorial tone.

VALUE_KIND_UNSTATED.means: A series is measured in percent but has not said whether its values are shares, so anything collapsed beyond capacity would be added together.
VALUE_KIND_UNSTATED.repair: Set `valueKind` to "share" when each value is a proportion of its own whole, or to "amount" to confirm the values really do add up.

TITLE_DENSITY.means: Prominent title text is denser than the capability recommends for legibility.
TITLE_DENSITY.repair: Shorten the title or move supporting detail into secondary copy.

SCENE_BELOW_RECOMMENDED_DURATION.means: A scene clears its hard duration floor but has less time than its recommended pacing.
SCENE_BELOW_RECOMMENDED_DURATION.repair: Span more narration beats when the resulting slower presentation is preferable.

capabilities.name: BarChartScene
capabilities.summary: Comparison of discrete values across named categories.
useWhen: comparing quantities between named categories
showing a ranking
contrasting two to eight values
making one value in a set stand out
avoidWhen: continuous change over time → line_chart
share of a whole → stat_donut
a single value → stat_counter
a sequence of dated events → timeline

title.description: Headline shown above the chart. Best under 40 characters; beyond that the type scale drops a step automatically.

label.description: Category name shown under the bar.

value.description: Plotted value. Negative values recompute the axis.

data.description: Series to compare. Best between 2 and 8 entries. From 9 to 20 the weakest are collapsed into a single 'Others' bar. An empty array renders a typographic empty state rather than a blank frame.

unit.description: Suffix appended to every value, e.g. '%' or '€'. Empty for bare numbers.

valueKind.description: What the numbers are, which decides what happens to the ones that do not fit. 'amount' is a count, a sum of money, a quantity: values beyond the capacity collapse into a single 'Others' bar carrying their total. 'share' is a percentage or a proportion, where each value is a share of its own whole — adding them would invent a category, so they are dropped instead and the chart shows fewer bars. Set this whenever `unit` is a percentage.

gridlines.description: Draw the value axis behind the bars. On, the axis states every value and only the highlighted bar prints its own number. Off, the axis disappears and every bar prints its number instead — choose that when the shot is short, when the chart shares the row with a callout, or when the exact figures are the point. Ignored by the horizontal layout, which is a ranking and never draws an axis.

highlight.description: The `label` of the bar to bring forward. Every other bar recedes toward the background. Must match a label present in `data`.

emphasis.description: Semantic reading of the highlighted value. Selects the accent role from the theme; never a raw colour.

data.onExceed: On the full canvas, values ranked below the top 8 are collapsed. A scene that yields into a half frame holds fewer — see `capacityByComposition`, which publishes the figure for every composition and layout — and collapses to that number instead. What collapsing does depends on `valueKind`: an 'amount' gathers the rest into a single 'Others' bar carrying their total, a 'share' drops them, because adding proportions of different wholes would invent a category.
data.onEmpty: Typographic empty state showing the title alone.

title.onExceed: Title drops one step of the type scale.

layouts.description: Vertical columns under a headline. The default reading order.
Horizontal bars with labels on the left. Use for long category names or for a ranking.
Chart on the left, with an annotation column on the right that opens when an `annotate` event lands and stays closed before it. Use when the scene carries an `annotate` event.

actions.description: Reveal the first bar alone, as a reference point.
Reveal the remaining bars in a staggered cascade.
Bring one bar forward and recede all the others.
Show a short annotation pointing at one bar.

text.description: Annotation copy. Keep it under 50 characters.

examples.note: The canonical shape: baseline, cascade, then one value pulled forward.

props.title: Share of income spent on rent

examples.title: Annotated comparison
examples.note: Uses the withCallout layout: the chart holds the full row until the annotate event lands, then yields a column to it. Also the axis-down case — the chart gives up a third of the row, so five printed figures cost less width than a ruler plus its number column.

props.title: Median deposit needed for a first home

examples.note: Soft limits both breached: the weakest values collapse into 'Others' and the title drops a type step.

examples.title: Empty case — no data
examples.note: A missing series is a legitimate state. Renders a typographic frame, not a black screen.

capabilities.name: CharacterExplainerScene
capabilities.summary: One resolved character cutout that materially carries an explanation, given restrained graphic motion and paired with concise copy.
useWhen: letting one recognisable figure or mascot visibly carry an explanation
personifying a concept through a guide who holds the frame while the copy explains it
giving a narrated emphasis a brief, repeatable visual reaction on the figure
avoidWhen: a person who only appears as documentary context → image_context
attributing exact spoken words to a person → quote
a claim that gains nothing from a character → typographic_statement
comparing numeric categories → bar_chart
uninterrupted character continuity across unrelated SceneCapabilities; use a Persistent element declared on the Section → persistent

label.description: Optional short identity or role, like a caption name. Best under 24 characters.

headline.description: Optional concise claim the character carries. Best under 48 characters; longer copy drops down the type scale.

explanation.description: Optional supporting copy beside the character. Best under 160 characters; longer copy wraps onto more lines.

type.description: This scene composes with a figure, never a plate or a document.

subject.description: Visual subject in natural language. Never a path or URI.

treatment.description: A cutout or an illustration; a photograph or duotone does not read as a figure that can carry an explanation.

orientation.description: Portrait or square; a landscape subject is a scene, not a figure.

identityKey.description: Stable identity shared by requirements that must resolve to the same asset.

assetRequirement.description: Semantic character request resolved before compilation. One cutout or illustration, portrait or square; never a path or URI.

label.onExceed: Shorten the label; it names the character, it is not a second headline.

headline.onEmpty: The frame leans on the character, the label and the explanation; the copy column shows a designed pending note instead.
headline.onExceed: The headline steps down the type scale until the copy column fits it.

explanation.onExceed: The explanation wraps onto more lines and recedes further behind the headline.

layouts.description: A dominant contained character cutout standing on one side of the frame, a bounded copy column on the other. The proportions are the layout’s, never the plan’s.

actions.description: Bring the character cutout onto the frame. Use it to hold the figure back until the narration reaches it.
Bring the label, headline and explanation in, one after the other. Independent of revealCharacter; either order is legal.
A brief graphic pulse of the whole cutout — a restrained scale and tilt with its halo — that returns the figure to rest. It may repeat; the latest event restarts the gesture.

capabilities.name: ImageContextScene
capabilities.summary: Editorial image paired with concise context copy for openings and transitions.
useWhen: establishing a documentary subject with one strong image
providing visual context before or after a data scene
pairing a photo or illustration with a concise editorial claim
avoidWhen: comparing numeric categories → bar_chart
locating a place or route → map
presenting a typography-only statement → typographic_statement

headline.description: Editorial headline paired with the image. Best under 40 characters; longer copy reduces the type scale.

caption.description: Optional supporting context. Best under 120 characters.

type.description: Semantic kind of visual material required by the scene.

subject.description: Visual subject in natural language. Never a path or URI.

treatment.description: Editorial treatment requested from the Asset Resolver.

orientation.description: Composition the resolved asset should support.

identityKey.description: Stable identity shared by requirements that must resolve to the same asset.

assetRequirement.description: Semantic visual request resolved before compilation. Never provide a path or URI.

headline.onEmpty: The asset subject becomes the only visible context label.
headline.onExceed: The headline drops one step of the type scale.

caption.onExceed: Shorten the caption to preserve an image-led composition.

layouts.description: Editorial image on the left with a concise headline and optional caption on the right. Composed into half a frame, the same three slots stack: plate above, copy below.

actions.description: Bring the image plate onto the frame. Use it to hold the image back until the narration reaches its subject.
Bring the headline and caption in, one after the other, after the image.
Stamp one spoken word or short phrase over the image, as the narrator says it. It holds until the scene ends, or until a later emphasis replaces it.

text.description: A word or short phrase the narrator speaks in this beat. Keep it under 40 characters.

capabilities.name: LineChartScene
capabilities.summary: Continuous numeric change across ordered calendar dates.
useWhen: showing a trend, acceleration or slowdown over calendar time
showing how a numeric measure changed across a period
comparing one to three temporal series on one value axis
calling out a dated high, low or inflection
avoidWhen: comparing discrete named categories → bar_chart
showing one number → stat_counter
showing shares of a whole → stat_donut
showing dated events without a numeric measure → timeline
showing correlation between two numeric variables → scatter_plot

title.description: Headline above the trend. Best under 48 characters; longer copy steps down.

date.description: Observation date in strict YYYY-MM-DD form, interpreted at UTC midnight.

label.description: Concise authored date label shown on the x-axis and named by point actions.

points.description: Shared ordered time axis. Best between 3 and 16 observations; up to 36 remain fully plotted with sparse labels and markers.

label.description: Unique series name used by the legend, focus and annotation actions.

items.description: Finite value observed at the aligned point index.

values.description: Values aligned one-for-one with `points` in authored order.

series.description: One or two aligned temporal series are recommended; three remain renderable.

unit.description: Suffix applied consistently to axis, focus and annotation values, e.g. '%' or '°C'.

baseline.description: `zero` includes zero to avoid exaggerating ordinary change. `extent` uses observed bounds with headroom for narrow measures such as temperature or rates.

focus.description: Initial semantic focus. A point focus always belongs to a named series.

label.description: Optional point display label to focus within the named series.

points.onExceed: All observations and straight segments remain. Intermediate date labels and ordinary point markers thin deterministically; first, last, focused and annotated points stay labelled.
points.onEmpty: The title remains with a designed “No trend data available” empty state.

series.onExceed: The third series remains fully plotted and identified in the legend, but the shot carries higher visual density.

title.onExceed: Title drops through the shared type-fitting ladder to preserve the plot.

layouts.description: A title and optional legend above one proportional UTC plot. Point annotations stay inside the plot.

actions.description: Hold plot marks back, then draw the trend from earlier to later dates.
Bring one temporal series forward and clear any earlier point focus.
Focus one dated observation and show its exact date and formatted value.
Attach one concise explanatory note to a dated observation.

text.description: Concise annotation copy, up to 70 characters.

examples.note: One series, a zero baseline and proportional calendar spacing. The trend reveals automatically.

examples.note: The useful density boundary at 17 points and three series: every observation remains in the lines while intermediate labels and ordinary markers thin.

capabilities.name: QuoteScene
capabilities.summary: A single quotation set large, with who said it. The words are the frame.
useWhen: letting a person's own words carry the frame
handing the narration over to a testimony, verdict or declaration
slowing the film down for one sentence that deserves to stand alone
avoidWhen: comparing quantities between categories → bar_chart
pairing a claim with a photograph → image_context
making one number the story → stat_counter

quote.description: The quoted words, without quotation marks — the scene draws its own mark. Best under 110 characters; beyond that the type scale drops a step automatically. An empty string renders a typographic empty state.

attribution.description: Who said it, as a name or short identifier. Empty makes the quote anonymous — use that only when the narration itself names the speaker.

role.description: One line of context under the attribution, e.g. 'Housing minister, 2021–2024'. Empty for none.

eyebrow.description: Optional small label above the mark, e.g. 'The testimony'. Carries section context while the quote is held back.

quote.onEmpty: Typographic empty state; the frame shows a "quote pending" label.
quote.onExceed: The quote drops one step of the type scale.

attribution.onExceed: Shorten the attribution; it is a signature, not a bio.

role.onExceed: Shorten the role line; it is context, not a second quote.

eyebrow.onExceed: Shorten the eyebrow; it is a label, not copy.

layouts.description: Eyebrow over an oversized quotation mark, the quote at display scale, and the attribution below — centred, nothing else on the frame.

actions.description: Bring the quote onto the frame, with its mark and attribution. Use it to hold the words back until the narration hands over to them; until then the eyebrow carries the frame.

capabilities.name: StatCounterScene
capabilities.summary: A single number set large, with what it counts. The figure is the frame.
useWhen: making one number the story
letting a single figure land on its own
stating a statistic the narration has just said aloud
avoidWhen: comparing quantities between categories → bar_chart
pairing a claim with a photograph → image_context
letting a person's own words carry the frame → quote

value.description: The number the frame carries, as a number — the scene formats it. An agent writing "1 in 3" is choosing typography the design system owns.

label.description: What the number counts, in one line. Always present — a number without a referent is the failure this scene exists to avoid.

unit.description: The unit set beside the value at a smaller step, e.g. '%', 'k', '°C'. Empty for a bare count.

sublabel.description: One supporting line under the label, e.g. 'up from 19% in 2005'. Empty for none.

emphasis.description: The semantic role the value reads in — its colour. Neutral for a plain figure.

label.onEmpty: Typographic empty state; the frame shows a "stat pending" label.
label.onExceed: The label drops one step of the type scale.

sublabel.onExceed: Shorten the sublabel; it is support, not a second claim.

unit.onExceed: Shorten the unit; it is a suffix, not a word.

layouts.description: The value at display scale, its unit beside it, and what it counts beneath — centred, nothing else on the frame.

actions.description: Bring the stat onto the frame. Use it to hold the number back until the narration says it; until then the label carries the frame.

capabilities.name: TimelineScene
capabilities.summary: A sequence of dated events in the order they happened, carrying no numeric measure.
useWhen: showing a chronology of dated events
showing how long a named period lasted and what fell inside it
showing that two moments are separated by a silence
situating a decision, a ruling or an announcement in time
avoidWhen: showing a numeric measure that moves over time → line_chart
comparing discrete named categories → bar_chart
showing a single figure, dated or not → stat_counter
showing ordered steps that carry no dates → diagram

title.description: Headline above the chronology. Best under 48 characters; longer copy steps down.

date.description: Date the event happened, in strict YYYY-MM-DD form, interpreted at UTC midnight.

label.description: What happened, set as display type and named by `focusEvent` and `annotate`. Must be unique within the scene.

events.description: The chronology, in strictly ascending date order. Authored order is binding and is never sorted. Best between 3 and 6 events; more remain drawn with their labels stacked.

periods.description: Named stretches of time drawn as continuous things rather than as pairs of events. One is the ordinary case; two remain drawable.

label.description: What the marked stretch of time is, e.g. "Rent cap in force".

from.description: First day of the period, in strict YYYY-MM-DD form.

to.description: Last day of the period, in strict YYYY-MM-DD form. Never before `from`.

events.onExceed: Every event keeps its mark on the axis at its proportional date. Crowded intermediate labels stack onto a second lane and then thin deterministically, leaving the mark without its words; the first, last, focused and annotated events stay labelled on the lane nearest the axis.
events.onEmpty: The title remains with a designed “No dated events available” empty state.

periods.onExceed: Both periods are drawn in full. Two bands on one axis read as one striped stretch of time unless the periods are far apart.

title.onExceed: Title drops through the shared type-fitting ladder to preserve the axis.

layouts.description: A horizontal axis where distance is elapsed time, so the gap between two events is information rather than composition. Use when how long something took is part of what the chronology says.

actions.description: Hold the chronology back, then reveal its events in date order.
Bring one dated event forward and let the rest of the chronology recede.
Attach one durable explanation to a dated event, and leave it up.

capabilities.name: TypographicStatementScene
capabilities.summary: One sentence set across a coloured ground that fills the frame. The chapter card that divides a film into movements.
useWhen: opening an act, chapter or movement, and saying what it is about
marking the turn in an argument, where the film changes register
stating a thesis in the film’s own voice, between two runs of evidence
avoidWhen: setting a person’s own words → quote
making one number the story → stat_counter
pairing a claim with a photograph → image_context

statement.description: The sentence the chapter is about, without quotation marks — this is the film speaking, not a person. Best under 72 characters; beyond that the type steps down the scale until it fits the band the layout reserves. An empty string renders a typographic empty state.

eyebrow.description: Optional small label above the statement, e.g. 'Chapter two'. It carries the frame on its own while `revealStatement` holds the sentence back.

ordinal.description: Where this chapter sits, as you want it read: '02 / 05', 'II', 'Part three'. Set small in mono at the foot of the frame. Nothing derives or checks it — the plan has no act model — so a wrong ordinal renders exactly as a right one.

emphasis.description: Semantic reading of the chapter this card opens. Selects the ground role from the theme; never a raw colour.

statement.onEmpty: Typographic empty state; the frame shows a "statement pending" label.
statement.onExceed: The statement steps down the type scale until it fits the band the card reserves.

eyebrow.onExceed: Shorten the eyebrow; it is a label, not a second statement.

ordinal.onExceed: Shorten the ordinal; it is a page number, not a title.

layouts.description: The emphasis role taken to full bleed, with the eyebrow and the statement knocked out of it and centred, and the ordinal small in the bottom corner.

actions.description: Bring the sentence onto the frame. Use it to hold the statement back until the narration hands over to it; until then the eyebrow and the ground carry the card.

Move the voice on by one word: everything before it stands in full, the word itself takes the mark, and the rest of the sentence stays recessive. Write one per word, in spoken order — the n-th event advances the n-th statement word, so there is no payload to name. For a recorded take, anchor it to that same word with `word:`; otherwise use beat boundaries for coarse pacing. Write none and the whole sentence simply stands.
